title.en: Seared chicken thighs with lemon-butter pan sauce

whyThis.en: Pan sauce comes right after searing. It turns the brown bits left in your pan into a sauce.

concept.en: Fond is the browned layer stuck to the pan after searing. Liquid loosens it, simmering makes it stronger, and cold butter swirled in at the end makes it glossy.

text.en: Pat the chicken thighs dry and salt both sides. Lay them skin-side down in a hot pan with the oil. Leave them alone until the skin is deep golden.

tip.en: Dry skin browns. Wet skin steams.

text.en: Flip the thighs and keep cooking until they are cooked through, with no pink at the thickest part. Move them to a plate.

tip.en: Not sure? Cut into the thickest thigh and look.

text.en: Pour off most of the fat. Add the minced garlic and stir until it smells sweet.

tip.en: Keep the brown bits in the pan. That is your fond.

text.en: Pour in the wine and scrape the pan with a wooden spoon until the brown bits lift.

tip.en: This is deglazing, the move you came for.

text.en: Let it bubble until about half is left.
Take the pan off the heat. Whisk in the cold butter and the juice of the lemon half. Taste, then add salt if it needs it.

tip.en: Off the heat, so the butter turns the sauce glossy instead of greasy.

text.en: Wilt the spinach in the same pan. Plate it with the chicken and spoon the sauce over.

question.en: What does the wine do when it hits the hot pan?

answers.en: It loosens the browned bits so they become the sauce
It cleans the pan so you can start again

explanation.en: The browned bits hold most of the flavor. Liquid lifts them off the pan and carries them into the sauce.
